Here at my observer site in Tok we have gotten 4.5 of snow since last evening at 8 pm_ when the snowfall first began. It is fine grained snow coming down fairly steadily and now fairly heavily. It was fairly thin and sparse last evening but is now heavier. - Katy in Tok.
Moderate to heavy snowfall_ 6 in by 10:50 am_ snowfall rates of about 1.5 to 2 in per hour. Current temp around 30 F with a light wind.
4 inches in North Pole! - Allison McCumber from Facebook.
Right about 4.5 by 6:30am this morning 10/21/26_ at 14.5 mile CHSR - Denise DeVoll from Facebook.
4 3/4 off ski boot - Mike McDonald from Facebook.
5 inches at my house_ off badger road NP - Jessica Benson from Facebook.
5.75 Gilmore & Gold Mine - Tim Armstrong from Facebook.
Only around 3.5 inches on the top of Old Nenana Ridge past Ester - Kellie Kenny-Obrien from Facebook.
Clearwater Road_ Delta at 0600_ oct 21... just over 5 settled snow_ very heavy - Sebastian P. Saarloos from Facebook.
5.75 of total snowfall near Shannon Park neighborhood. Still lightly snowing. - Matt Phelps from Facebook.
Little over 5 up on Birch Hill as of 8:30am October 21st_ still snowing - Pam Watson from Facebook.
5 off Steele Creek. At 8:45am October 21. We got 3 of that 5 last night - Karen Schauer from Facebook.
Current conditions: Temperatures 18.6 degrees Humidity 87% Barometer 29.72 rising rapidly Wind calm.
Spotter (Kathy Turk) reported snow began 20:00 AKDT 10/19 and ended 17:00 AKDT 10/20. Additional light snow occurred the morning of the 21st bringing the total to 9.5.
Snow began in earnest Tuesday around 2 pm.

Robyn Russell reporting from 41 Eureka Ave in Hamilton Acres (Fairbanks_ AK). Received about 4.5-5.5 of snow (measuring at different places in my yard). Snow damp_ but not wet. Sun out_ snow melting in sunny spots_ light snow (diamond dust) continuing to fall as of 10/21/26 at 1:50 p.m.
Gusts greater than 35mph with visibility one quarter mile or less from about Noon to 4pm. Maximum gust 48 mph at 3:45pm.
Gusts greater than 35mph with visibility near one quarter mile or less from around 1pm to 4 pm. Max wind gust during this period 48 mph at 2:05pm AKDT.

Strong wind gusts up to around 60 mph impacted a powerline and has left a large portion of Kivalina without power. Residents are being shuttled to the new school_ and about 175 people stayed there Friday night. It may be up to a week before power returns. They are prepping medical supplies in case they need to fly the injured to Kotzebue.

candidate_reports.remark: Six inches of snow fell at Nome Beltz Jr/Sr High School before transitioning to rain as of Friday evening around 6:30 PM.

Multiple public reports of coastal flooding in Hooper Bay with roads inundated_ impacting access to the airfield. Water levels per P-ETSS guidance shows a peak around 4 to 6 feet above the normal high tide line around 2 PM AKDT with gusts up to around 60 mph observed. Water levels are expected to drop to around 2 to 4 feet Friday night into Saturday.

Multiple public reports of coastal flooding in Teller with roads inundated and outlying structures impacted. Water levels per P-ETSS guidance show a peak around 3 to 5 feet above the normal high tide line Friday afternoon through Saturday with gusts up to around 60 mph observed. Water levels are expected to drop to around 2 to 4 feet Sunday into Monday.

Public report of coastal flooding in Wales with roads inundated and outlying structures impacted. Water levels per P-ETSS guidance show a peak around 3 to 5 feet above the normal high tide line Friday through Saturday with gusts up to around 70 mph observed. Water levels are expected to drop to around 2 to 4 feet Sunday into Monday.
The Bettles COOP site recorded 7 inches of new snow in the past 24 hours with a 13 inch snow depth. Snow is continuing to fall as of Sunday morning.
The Wiseman COOP site recorded 6.8 inches of new snow in the past 24 hours. Snow is continuing to fall as of Sunday morning.
Alaska DOT 511 reported 6 to 8 inches of new snow along the Elliott Highway from MP 110 to MP 138 with very difficult travel conditions ongoing.
ASOS station PANN in Nenana recorded light freezing rain Monday morning_ with up 0.03 inches as of 11 AM.
3.1 inches of snow fell at the NWS Fairbanks office on the UAF campus as of 12 PM with snow continuing to fall.
Social media report showing a ruler in 6 inches of snow.
Near the intersection of Chena Pump and Chena Point Road.
Social media report of rain making roads very icy in Anderson. Unknown accumulation.

Public report from Goldstream on the east side of Moose Mountain at about 900 feet elevation via Facebook. Report specified that the temperature rose to just below freezing and the snow turned to the consistency of wet sand.
Snow is now mixing with light rain as precipitation comes to an end.

It kept snowing heavily until around 6pm_ when it transitioned to rain. I didn't take a sample for SWE yesterday_ and when I measured this morning_ it had compacted to 4.3" of fresh snow. My gauge catch was 0.61" total.
